interactions.label: A 28-year-old woman presents with an itchy, widespread, ill-defined erythematous

params.question: A 28-year-old woman presents with an itchy, widespread, ill-defined erythematous rash on her trunk after three weeks of using a combination cream containing betamethasone and clotrimazole. Which feature makes performing a KOH mount most critical before starting systemic antifungals?

answers.text: The rash is located on the trunk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While trunk lesions can be fungal, location alone does not make KOH most critical. The key trigger here is that steroid use has altered the morphology, making visual diagnosis unreliable.

answers.text: She has been using a steroid-containing cream that may have altered the lesion morphology

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Steroid misuse creates tinea incognito, masking the classic ring-shaped appearance. KOH confirmation is most critical when prior treatment has distorted the clinical picture and your eyes can no longer be trusted.

answers.text: The rash has been present for three weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Duration alone does not determine the need for KOH. The test is most critical when prior treatment has distorted the clinical picture, regardless of how long the rash has been present.

Itching and extent are important clinical features but do not specifically make KOH most critical. The decisive factor is that steroid use has altered the lesion's morphology, making clinical diagnosis unreliable.

overallFeedback.feedback: When prior steroid use alters a lesion's appearance, clinical pattern recognition fails — this is exactly when KOH confirmation is most critical before starting systemic antifungals.
Steroid-modified tinea (tinea incognito) masks classic features, making KOH confirmation indispensable before committing to systemic therapy.

interactions.label: A student performs a KOH mount by scraping scales from the central clearing of a

params.question: A student performs a KOH mount by scraping scales from the central clearing of a ring-shaped groin lesion. The mount shows no fungal elements. What is the most likely reason for this false-negative result?

answers.text: The KOH concentration used was too high, destroying the hyphae

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Standard 10–20% KOH clears keratin without destroying chitin-walled fungal structures. Overheating, not high KOH concentration, is what creates artefacts and damages hyphae.

answers.text: The centre of the annular lesion has already started clearing and contains few viable fungi

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! In a ring-shaped dermatophyte lesion, viable fungus concentrates at the active, advancing edge. The centre has already started clearing, yielding little or no organism — a classic cause of false-negative KOH mounts.

answers.text: The coverslip was not pressed firmly enough on the slide

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While an uneven mount can make microscopy harder, it would not explain a complete absence of fungal elements. The problem here is the sampling site, not slide preparation technique.

answers.text: The microscope magnification was set too low to detect hyphae

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Initial scanning at 10× followed by 40× confirmation is standard and adequate to detect hyphae. The issue is that insufficient viable fungus was collected from the cleared centre of the lesion.

overallFeedback.feedback: In annular lesions, the centre has started clearing and harbours few organisms. Always sample the active, scaly, advancing edge to avoid this classic false-negative pitfall.
The active, advancing edge is where dermatophytes concentrate — always scrape the margin, not the centre, for a reliable KOH mount.

params.question: A patient presents with beefy-red, moist plaques in the inguinal folds with small pustules scattered around the edges. Which diagnosis is most consistent with this clinical picture?

answers.text: Tinea cruris — erythematous scaly plaques with an advancing edge

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tinea cruris typically shows dry, scaly, annular plaques with a well-defined, raised margin. It lacks the beefy-red moistness and satellite pustules that characterise candidal infection in skin folds.

answers.text: Pityriasis versicolor — finely scaly hypo- or hyperpigmented macules

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pityriasis versicolor presents as finely scaly patches on the trunk and shoulders that are lighter or darker than surrounding skin. It does not produce moist, beefy-red plaques with pustules in body folds.

answers.text: Cutaneous candidiasis — beefy-red rash with satellite pustules in skin folds

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Beefy-red, moist plaques in body folds with satellite pustules at the periphery are the hallmark of cutaneous candidiasis — a key feature that distinguishes it from the dry, scaly plaques of tinea cruris.

answers.text: Tinea corporis — annular plaque with central clearing on the trunk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tinea corporis forms ring-shaped, scaly plaques with an active raised margin and central clearing, typically on the trunk or limbs. It does not produce the beefy-red, moist appearance with satellite pustules described here.

overallFeedback.feedback: Beefy-red, moist plaques in body folds with satellite pustules point to cutaneous candidiasis, not tinea. Tinea cruris produces dry, scaly plaques with a raised, advancing edge — a different morphology entirely.
Satellite pustules around beefy-red, moist plaques in skin folds are the hallmark of cutaneous candidiasis — a crucial distinction from tinea cruris in the groin.

interactions.label: When oral terbinafine fails in chronic recurrent tinea, the appropriate next ste

params.question: When oral terbinafine fails in chronic recurrent tinea, the appropriate next step is to repeat terbinafine at a higher dose or for a longer duration.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Repeating or escalating terbinafine is not the answer when resistance is the cause. Squalene epoxidase mutations in Indian dermatophytes make dose escalation futile. The correct step is to switch to oral itraconazole and stop any topical steroid combination creams that drive resistance.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! Terbinafine resistance due to squalene epoxidase mutations is now widespread among Indian dermatophytes. When first-line terbinafine fails, the evidence-based step is to switch to oral itraconazole — not to repeat or escalate terbinafine. Stopping topical steroid combination creams is equally important, as these drive spread and resistance.
